subject: fennec
pitch: A fennec fox kit standing alert on a little sand dune at dusk. Enormous satin ears lined in pale peach, cream fur warming to sandy gold along its back, a fluffy tail with a smudge of black at the tip, and big dark eyes with a tiny white sparkle. Its paws are a touch oversized, like it hasn't grown into them yet, and it wears a woven leather collar with a small brass bell.
reasoning:
I'm planning the scale of the fennec fox kit model, sizing its body, shoulders, and oversized ears in meters, and deciding that the sand dune base should be included as part of the scene with its lowest point sitting at y=0.

Now I'm sketching out the construction plan: a seeded RNG helper, a palette of materials (cream fur, sandy gold, peach ear lining, black, dark eyes, brass, sand), and the approach of using vertex colors on the torso sphere to blend cream belly fur into golden back fur rather than relying on textures. I'm also working out the placement and scaling of the head, snout, and nose geometry relative to the body.

Next I'm figuring out the ears as flattened ellipsoids with an outer sandy layer and inner peach lining, positioning them on the head with slight outward and forward tilts for an alert look, then calculating eye placement using the head sphere's surface geometry so the dark pupils and tiny white sparkle highlights sit correctly on the face without clipping through the skull.

Now I'm working out the legs and dune base: thin cylindrical legs for the fennec, and a flattened sphere forming the sand dune the fox stands on, adjusting the dune's vertical scale and center position so its bottom stays at or near ground level while the fox sits properly on its crest.

Then I'm placing the body as an ellipsoid at y=0.38, aligning the leg heights to connect seamlessly with it, and positioning the head and eyes relative to the body's front edge, calculating exact coordinates for the snout and eye surface positions.

Now I'm sizing the oversized fennec ears and working out their rotation—figuring out which axis and sign tilts each ear outward and slightly forward so they flare symmetrically from the top of the head.

For the inner ear detail, I'm deciding to keep each ear as a simple group with two unscaled-position meshes (outer and inner ellipsoids) rather than nesting scaled geometry, since nonuniform mesh scale would distort any child transforms if I tried to parent them.

Working out the exact z-offsets and radii so the inner ellipse pokes through the outer ear's front face rather than being hidden inside it, then nudging the inner lining downward slightly so it doesn't reach the ear tip. For the tail, I'm planning a curved chain of four or five spheres with growing radii, plotting a rough path curving up and back behind the body.

Now sizing the tail segments and coloring the first few in the body's fur tone, with the last segment or tip sphere switching to black. I'm also figuring out where the collar torus sits around the neck, using the body ellipsoid's cross-section math at the neck's z-position to size the torus radius appropriately.

For the collar itself, I'm placing a stylized torus loop around the neck with a slight tilt since the neck axis runs diagonally, then adding a tiny brass bell sphere hanging at the ring's bottom.

For legs, I'm positioning four at symmetric x offsets with front/back z spacing, giving oversized elongated paw shapes near the ground. For the dune, I'll keep it minimal without extra pebbles or tufts, and I'm picking a cream belly fur color against a richer gold back tone, using vertex colors for the blend.

I'm setting up a smoothstep gradient based on local vertex height to shade gold at the top and cream at the bottom of the body, extending the same blended vertex-coloring approach to the head mesh. The material uses standard vertex coloring with fairly rough, matte shading.

Now I'm scaffolding the module with metadata and a seeded random number generator, planning to use it for scattering a couple dozen tiny sand-grain spheres across the dune's surface using polar coordinates on a hemisphere.

I'm defining the full material palette: fur with vertex colors, satiny gold and peach tones for the ears, deep black and dark eye colors with a white sparkle highlight, leather, brass with high metalness, sand, and a cream tone for the paws, while leaving the lighting/fog decisions for later since they're outside the model itself. I'm also writing a small ellipsoid-mesh helper function to simplify placing scaled, rotated sphere primitives throughout the model.

I'm now writing a gradient vertex-color function that blends a top and bottom color across the mesh based on local y-position using a smoothstep, applying it to the body (cream to gold) and head with slightly different thresholds, then starting the main build function with a flattened dune-shaped base mesh.

I'm sizing the dune relative to the fox's small scale and figuring out how to position the fox group's legs so they sit properly embedded into the dune's crest, adjusting the y-offset so the body coordinates work out correctly against the dune height.

Still adjusting fox body coordinates...

Working through eye placement with sparkle highlights and proper protrusion through the head surface, nose sizing and position, and planning the tail segments with a gradient fur material to match the body.

Sketching out a helper function for creating fur spheres with vertex-color gradients, then laying out the five tail segments with decreasing radii and a black tip sphere at the end.

I'm deciding on the color scheme — cream to sandy-gold gradient along the body, head, and tail, with paws kept a flat cream tone separately. Then I'm planning the sand grain scattering using a seeded random generator, placing roughly 22 grains across the dune with polar coordinates for natural clustering.

I'm also working out the collar: a leather torus positioned around the neck, calculating the rotation needed so the ring's normal aligns with the neck's actual direction between body and head.

The bell hangs from the bottom of that ring, so I'm computing where the ring's lowest point sits in 3D space and placing a small brass sphere there, visible at the front of the chest. For the woven look, I'm considering layering a second, thinner torus in a darker tone over the collar to suggest stitching or braiding.

Now I'm setting up the ear rotations with tilted Euler angles so they angle outward naturally, then planning the geometry helper function that builds ellipsoids for each body part. I'm deciding that all the furry parts (body, head, tail, paws) will share one fur material using vertex colors for gradient shading, so I need a helper that assigns gradient colors per-vertex based on height, with paws using a cream gradient between top and bottom tones.

Writing material setup...

Writing blob helper function...

Setting up the dune mesh with a seeded random generator, then thinking about adding a secondary blob to make the dune shape asymmetric and more wind-swept looking.

Still working out the geometry for the dune blobs...

For the grains, I'm scattering tiny half-embedded spheres across the ellipsoid surface using normalized radius and angle to compute position, keeping them low-poly for performance. Now I'm setting up the fox as a group positioned on top of the dune, aligning its internal coordinate system so the paws sit correctly relative to the dune's peak height.

Moving to the legs, I'm using tapered cylinders for front and back legs with slightly different thickness, placing oversized cream-colored paw blobs at the leg bottoms that are proportionally wider than the leg radius to get that "oversized" kit look. For the body I'm layering a large furred blob with a gradient to cream for the belly, then adding a neck blob to bridge to the head, a slightly wide head blob, optional cheek puffs in cream, a tapered snout blob extending forward, and a tiny black nose sphere at the snout tip.

For the ears, I'm building symmetric groups positioned and rotated outward and forward on each side, each containing a thin wide-tall outer ellipsoid as the ear shape and a smaller inner ellipsoid offset slightly forward to represent the ear's inner coloring, checking that the rotations correctly tilt the ear tops outward and forward. Now I'm moving on to the tail pieces and a leather collar made from a torus shape.

I'm positioning a torus around the neck for the collar, calculating where a small brass bell sphere should hang below the ring based on the ring's geometry, and confirming the collar sits properly on the neck blob. I'm finalizing the fur and material logic so gradients only apply to fur geometry while the tail tip stays solid black, then writing out the complete scene.
